title: Participle Mastery
intro: At C1 level, participles become a powerful tool for sophisticated expression. PARTICIPLE VS КОТОРЫЙ: Participles are more formal/literary; который is neutral/conversational. POSITIONING: Attributive (before noun) vs. predicative (after noun with commas). AGREEMENT: Participles agree in gender, number, case with their noun. PASSIVE SHORT FORMS: Used predicatively (Книга прочитана). STYLISTIC CHOICE: Academic/literary texts prefer participles; spoken Russian prefers который. Master participle usage for elegant, concise expression.
rules: Attributive position: читающий студент (the reading student)
Predicative position: студент, читающий книгу, ... (the student, reading a book, ...)
Short passive = predicative only: Книга прочитана (The book has been read)
examples: Студент, читающий книгу, сидит у окна. (The student reading the book is sitting by the window.)
Прочитанная книга лежит на столе. (The read book is lying on the table.)
Написанное вчера письмо уже отправлено. (The letter written yesterday has already been sent.)
Вопрос, обсуждаемый на собрании, очень важен. (The question being discussed at the meeting is very important.)

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Passive past participle: прочитанная (that was read)
hints: The book was read (completed action, passive). Which participle type is formed from a perfective verb and describes a completed passive action?
explanations: Passive past participle 'прочитанная' (that was read/having been read) is formed from perfective 'прочитать.' It agrees with 'книга' (feminine). Active participle 'прочитавшая' means 'who read' (not passive), and present participles don't express completed actions.
